html:
The largest of the hundreds of ancient water tanks under Istanbul, built by Justinian after the Nika riots of 532, under a great public hall called the Basilica, a short walk from Hagia Sophia.

It is a vast underground room about 138 m by 65 m. Its roof is held up by 336 marble columns, each about 9 m high, in twelve rows, many of them reused from older buildings. Two columns stand on carved heads of Medusa, one upside down and one on its side. The tank held water brought by the Aqueduct of Valens and supplied the Great Palace and nearby buildings, a store against siege and drought.

The Ottomans kept using it for a time, but it was largely forgotten above ground. In the 1540s a French scholar found it after learning that people were drawing water and even catching fish through holes in their basements. Today it is a museum.
sum: The largest of the hundreds of ancient water tanks under Istanbul, built by Justinian after the Nika riots of 532, under a great public hall called the Basilica, a short walk from Hagia Sophia.
